run.question: We're running low on disk space. Can you check our application indexes (app-187-*) and identify which one is consuming the most storage? Please tell me the index name and approximately how much space it's using.

report.summary: Among the 21 indices matching app-187-*, the one consuming the most storage is app-187-metrics-analytics: 519,024 bytes store size (~507 KiB, ~0.52 MB) with 5,000 documents, health green. Two independent views (index listing and index stats) agree exactly on that figure, and its primary and total store sizes are identical (no replicas allocated). The other 20 indices are the log indices app-187-logs-01..20, each holding 10 documents and ~9.3 KB: 19 of them at 9,275 bytes and app-187-logs-02 at 9,377 bytes. The entire set of app-187-* indices totals 704,626 bytes (~688 KiB), and that same 704,626-byte total is what index_stats reports for _all. So the largest application index uses about half a megabyte, and all app-187-* indices together use under 1 MiB. Counter to the premise of disk pressure: the single Elasticsearch node bea971fdc0c6 reports 149.4 GB total disk, 59.2 GB used (39.66%) and 90.1 GB available, with heap at 20% — no disk-space exhaustion is visible at query time. The cluster's yellow status comes from 20 unassigned shards on a 1-data-node cluster (replicas that cannot be allocated), which shows up as yellow health on the 20 log indices; it is an allocation/redundancy condition, not a storage-size condition. No fault is identified here, so no root cause is named; the findings are capacity observations at the moment of the query (observed_at 2026-11-23T17:39:59Z to 17:40:11Z). If real disk pressure exists it is not coming from app-187-* indices, and its source was not located in this run.

claims.text: app-187-metrics-analytics is the largest of the 21 app-187-* indices: store.size 519,024 bytes (~507 KiB, ~0.52 MB), 5,000 docs, health green, status open, and pri.store.size equal to store.size (519,024), i.e. no replica copy counted.

The remaining 20 app-187-* indices are the log indices app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20, every one with 10 documents and health yellow: 19 of them have store.size 9,275 bytes and app-187-logs-02 has 9,377 bytes (index_stats: 8,900 bytes of document data, 9,377 total store).

Total store size across the app-187-* indices is 704,626 bytes (~688 KiB); the same 704,626-byte figure is reported for _all primaries and _all total in index_stats, and an index listing with pattern "*" returned the same 21 indices with the same sizes and 0 indices omitted.

The single Elasticsearch node bea971fdc0c6 (role cdfhilmrstw) reports disk.total 149.4gb, disk.used 59.2gb, disk.used_percent 39.66, disk.avail 90.1gb and heap.percent 20 at query time, so low free disk space is not visible at the node holding these indices.

Cluster health is yellow with 24 active primary shards, 24 active shards (active_shards_percent 54.545...) and 20 unassigned shards on number_of_data_nodes 1 and number_of_nodes 1, which matches the yellow health of the 20 app-187-logs-* indices as unassigned replica shards rather than index size.

If the reported disk pressure is real, its source is outside the app-187-* indices and outside the Elasticsearch index store measured here (_all store total 704,626 bytes), for example node-level non-index files, container image layers or another volume on the host; the evidence gathered does not identify which, so this remains unverified.

Treat app-187-metrics-analytics as the index to look at first if app-187-* pruning is needed, but note that reclaiming it would free only ~507 KiB; for real disk relief, inspect the node's non-index disk usage (disk.used 59.2gb vs index store ~688 KiB) and host volumes with tools that can see the filesystem or host metrics.

gaps: Cluster health reports 24 active primary shards while index_stats for _all and the index listings account for 21 indices / 21 primaries (41 shards total including replicas); the extra primaries were not enumerated and could belong to hidden or system indices that these views do not list as of query time.

No host filesystem or volume metrics (node exporter, kubelet imagefs/eviction signals) were examined, so the origin of the stated disk pressure was not located; the Elasticsearch node view shows 90.1gb available at query time.

Index sizes are point-in-time readings at observed_at 2026-11-23T17:39:59Z-17:40:11Z; size growth over time and deleted-document overhead (5,200 deleted docs across the indices) were not analyzed with a time series, so trends are unknown.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether an index, template or lifecycle policy changed recently could not be checked.
next_steps: Confirm which filesystem or volume is actually reported as low (host path, PV, or container layer) before deleting any index, since app-187-* totals under 1 MiB.
If log-index pruning is desired, consider reviewing the 20 app-187-logs-* indices' retention/ILM settings; deleting all 20 would free roughly 186 KB.
If replica-shard health matters, add a second data node or set the log indices' replica count to 0 on this single-node cluster to clear the 20 unassigned shards.
